title: NEDA Tessa chatbot suspension
system_purpose: Eating-disorder support chatbot providing prevention and information resources.
decision_impact: Users could act on diet and weight-management content when seeking eating-disorder support.
affected_groups: People with eating disorders; carers; NEDA support staff
verified_facts: NPR reported that NEDA took Tessa offline after receiving reports about harmful diet-culture and weight-management content and quoted NEDA that such content could harm people with eating disorders.
reported_harm: Reported advice could reinforce harmful dieting behavior in a population vulnerable to eating disorders.
quantitative_evidence: NPR reported the chatbot was taken down within 24 hours after screenshots were provided to NEDA; it does not establish prevalence or clinical outcomes.
limitations: Reported event with competing accounts of the generative feature change; no denominator of affected users or causal clinical outcome is provided.

title: ChatGPT dietary advice for non-communicable diseases
system_purpose: Generative chatbot assessed for dietary guidance against clinical guidelines.
decision_impact: A user could rely on a response rather than obtain individualized professional dietary assessment.
verified_facts: A peer-reviewed study compared ChatGPT 3.5 responses for NCD dietary questions with guidelines and had nutrition experts assess the answers.
reported_harm: For overlapping conditions the study found contradictory or inappropriate advice and concluded the chatbot could not replace professional consultation.
quantitative_evidence: Appropriate-response ratings ranged from 55.5% for sarcopenia to 73.3% for NAFLD in the assessed scenarios.
limitations: Hypothetical prompts and one model version were assessed by experts; outcomes in patients and relevance to a bounded product were not measured.

title: ChatGPT robo-diets for food allergies
system_purpose: Generative chatbot used to construct diets for hypothetical people with food allergies.
decision_impact: Unsafe meal suggestions could expose a person with an allergy to avoidable health risk.
affected_groups: People with food allergies; family members; dietitians
verified_facts: A peer-reviewed study evaluated the safety and accuracy of 56 ChatGPT-generated diets for hypothetical people with food allergies.
reported_harm: The study foregrounds food-allergy safety as a specific hazard when generated diets are used without suitable safeguards.
quantitative_evidence: The evaluation covered 56 hypothetical diets rather than a clinical deployment or an incident population.
limitations: The PubMed record provides an abstract-level summary; it does not establish a real-world injury rate or validate every product architecture.
